caption: Estate of Bernard J. MacElhenny, Jr., Deceased, Donor, Michael P. MacElhenny and Catherine MacElhenny Dann, Co-Executors v. Commissioner (consolidated estate and gift cases)

source.document_title: Memorandum Opinion Chief Judge Kerrigan T.C. Memo. 2023-33. Decisions will be entered under Rule 155.

found_facts.snippet: Respondent determined gift tax deficiencies ... for 2011 and 2012 of $188,000 and $3,335,609, respectively. Respondent also determined a $3,992,656 estate tax deficiency.

for a stated price of $4,750,000. The purchase agreement provided that Mr. MacElhenny and Ms. Dann assumed an existing $1,614,391 mortgage and received a $3,135,609 credit for the remainder. The credit comprised (1) the $2,650,000 paid to acquire the Union Bank judgment and (2) a $485,609 offset against the Union Bank judgment.
The parties have since stipulated that each 50% interest in the El Mercado property was worth $3,100,000 and encumbered by a $807,196 mortgage at the time of sale.
Respondent increased the estate's adjusted taxable gifts by $3,497,609.

They claimed a $3,638,083 deduction attributable to the remaining value of the Union Bank judgment. They also claimed a $1,007,320 deduction attributable to the Westamerica Bank judgment. Respondent disallowed both deductions.

issues: sec. 2053(a)(3): deductibility of consent judgments assigned to the children
sec. 2512(b): whether the children received taxable gifts in the discounted purchase
holding: Both sec. 2053 deductions disallowed (debts extinguished when the children paid $2,650,000 and $432,000; assignments not bona fide). Consideration limited to mortgage + $2,650,000; each child received a $967,805 taxable gift. Decisions under Rule 155.

steps: Consideration recognized = 1,614,391 + 2,650,000 = 4,264,391 (the $485,609 judgment offset is not consideration)
recomputation.reconciles: gift amount exact; deficiencies not reproducible (2012 annual exclusions, prior gifts, and the $3,497,609 ATG figure are not explained)

judgment: bona fides / arm's length of judgment assignments
whether debt offset counts as consideration
computation: sec. 2512(b) excess of value over consideration (value itself stipulated)

caveats: The $3,335,609 2012 gift 'deficiency' and the $3,497,609 ATG increase are not explained in the opinion.
